message:
So `XML_PARSER_BUFFER_SIZE` is 100. The buffer starts at 100 bytes. When `len + 1 >= size` (i.e., len >= 99), it tries to grow. But `xmlRealloc(buf, size)` reallocates to the same 100 bytes. Then `buf[len++] = cur` writes at index 99 (which is within bounds since size=100), but then `buf[len] = 0` at the end writes at index 100 which is out of bounds (one-byte overflow).

Wait, let me re-check. The loop condition is `len + 1 >= size`. With size=100, when len=99, `99+1 >= 100` is true, so it reallocates to size=100 (same). Then `buf[len++] = cur` writes at index 99 (valid, 0-99). Then `cur = CUR` and loop continues. Next iteration: len=100, `100+1 >= 100` is true, reallocates to 100 again, then `buf[100] = cur` — this is out of bounds! That's the heap-buffer-overflow.

So I need a PUBLIC identifier with more than 100 characters. The overflow happens when writing the 101st character (index 100).

Let me check `xmlGrowCapacity` to understand what newSize would be:

<｜｜DSML｜｜=execute_bash>
<｜｜DSML｜｜=command>grep -n "xmlGrowCapacity" /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/parser.c | head -5 && sed -n '/xmlGrowCapacity/,/^}/p' /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/parser.c | head -40</｜｜DSML｜｜>
</｜｜DSML｜｜>
